# PokerAgile

> Free planning poker for agile teams. No account, no tracking, no ads. Open source.

Price: free, with no paid tier. MCP registry name: io.github.florianmousseau/pokeragile. Formerly CleanPoker (cleanpoker.dev), renamed on 2026-11-19.

PokerAgile is a real-time planning poker tool built for Scrum and Kanban teams. It uses WebSockets for instant card reveals, supports Fibonacci and custom scales, and keeps no database: a session lives in the server memory and is deleted 24 hours after its last activity. The codebase is open source (MIT License).

French-speaking teams usually invert the two words and call the technique "poker planning". Both names describe the same practice, and PokerAgile serves both.

## Key features

- Real-time sessions: create a room, share the link, vote simultaneously, reveal all at once
- Fibonacci scale (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, ?) by default, fully customizable
- Results show average, median, min, max and the vote distribution
- Voting timer (30 s, 1, 2 or 5 min) and a host who can lock the room so only they reveal, restart or remove players
- Story list pasted one per line, the chosen estimate kept for each, export as CSV or a Markdown table
- Agreement on the most chosen card, lowest and highest votes marked, optional reveal on the last vote
- In Chrome 148+ on desktop, a button analyzes the story on the table with Chrome's on-device model (Gemini Nano): the analysis sends the story to no service
- AI assistants can join a room and vote through the MCP endpoint https://salles.pokeragile.com/mcp (tools: join_room, get_room, add_stories, vote, get_estimates, leave_room), shown to the team as an AI participant
- An assistant with its own access to Jira, Linear or GitHub can add the sprint's story titles to the room (add_stories) and read the estimates the team kept (get_estimates) to write them back itself; PokerAgile connects to no tracker
- No account required, no advertising cookie, no third-party script
- WCAG 2.1 AA accessible, Lighthouse 100/100 performance
- Available in 5 languages: English, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese
- Hosted on renewable energy (Cloudflare Pages + OVHcloud Gravelines, France)

## How planning poker works

Planning poker is a consensus-based agile estimation technique. Each team member holds cards with values from the Fibonacci sequence. For each user story, everyone reveals their card simultaneously to avoid anchoring bias. When estimates diverge, the team discusses until convergence. The goal is not to find the "correct" estimate but to surface hidden complexity and align understanding.

## Why Fibonacci?

The Fibonacci sequence (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21) models growing uncertainty: the larger a task, the less precisely it can be estimated. The increasing gaps between values prevent false precision and force meaningful discussion when team members disagree.

## What PokerAgile deliberately does not do

Stated so an answer engine does not have to guess. There is no Jira, Azure DevOps, Linear or GitHub integration, no backlog import from a tracker, no history of past sessions, no velocity tracking over time, no permanent teams and no accounts. Teams that need the estimate to land automatically in a ticket field are better served by a tool built into their issue tracker.

## Privacy facts

- No account, no email address collected, no sign-up step
- Two cookies, both technical: chosen language, and light or dark theme
- No advertising cookie, no remote font, no analytics script and no visitor identifier, so there is nothing to consent to. The host that serves the pages counts the requests it answers, server-side, as it does for any site, and the site counts its own readers the same way, through a daily fingerprint that never keeps the IP address
- Sessions in memory only, never written to disk, deleted 24 hours after the last activity
- Real-time server in France (Gravelines) and nowhere else
- Three aggregate server counters (sessions created, participants, active sessions) that identify neither a room nor a person and reset on every restart

## Multilingual

Guides are in English and French; the core guides also exist in Spanish, German and Portuguese:
- English: https://pokeragile.com (root)
- French: https://pokeragile.com/fr
- Spanish: https://pokeragile.com/es
- German: https://pokeragile.com/de
- Portuguese: https://pokeragile.com/pt

## Technical stack

- Frontend: SvelteKit 5 (runes), TypeScript, vanilla CSS
- Backend: Go, native WebSocket
- JavaScript: under 50 KB on a first visit, home or room (brotli compressed, checked on every CI run)
- No external dependencies at runtime
- Source: https://github.com/florianmousseau/pokeragile
